clue.text: Sidesman?

parts.note: read not as a churchwarden's helper but as a man who belongs to a sports side and works for it

explanation.walkthrough: A sidesman is an usher at an Anglican church service; the question mark invites reading it as 'a man of the side', someone who plays for the team rather than himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooperative member of a side who puts the group first is what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Go off course, and face the other way

explanation.surface: A traveller strays from the route and spins about.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversing direction means leaving one's course, and also means rotating to look behind.

clue.text: Not completely open initially about clash

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word about

parts.note: to clash is to jar, as discordant colours or sounds do

explanation.surface: A row that was only partly out in the open at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open, not shut and not fully swung back, is described this way.

clue.text: Vet finished, getting cross

parts.note: to vet something and approve it is to pass it
something finished is over

explanation.surface: A veterinary surgeon finishes the day in a bad mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor and 'cross' like angry; both shift sense, the first to 'check and approve', the second to 'go across'.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse or fly above something is to go across it.

clue.text: Hell for some out of work

definitions.text: Hell for some out of work

parts.words: Hell for some out of work
parts.note: describes the misery that unemployment brings to many people, a state of intense suffering

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a description: being jobless is torment for some, and the answer is the word for such torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme mental or physical suffering is likened to hell.

clue.text: Note torn slip attached to Greek letter

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: a torn slip has its pieces scattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: on means attached to, as a label is on a parcel

explanation.surface: A note on a ripped slip of paper fixed to a Greek character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'torn' makes PSIL from SLIP, between E and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet, used for small quantities in mathematics.

clue.text: They protest, and want record reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters of want record are gone over again in a new order

explanation.surface: Demonstrators who want their criminal record looked at again.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired mob paid to make up the numbers at a demonstration.

clue.text: A tense trial witness

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A nervous moment as someone gives evidence at a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness is to declare formally that something is true.

clue.text: Sale next door finally disposed of non-essential items

indicators.note: read as dis-posed, the letters placed in a different order
finally points to the last letter of door

explanation.surface: The garage sale next door got rid of things nobody needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' looks like getting rid of things, but it signals rearranging SALENEXT plus R, the last letter of 'door'.
explanation.definitionFit: Outward features as opposed to the core are inessential surface matters.

clue.text: River slime, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word spoken aloud matches the answer

parts.note: ooze is soft mud or slime

explanation.surface: A muddy river, judging by its name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, in York among other places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a name borne by several English waterways.

clue.text: Party member accepting man's hypothesis

indicators.note: the party member accepts, or takes in, the other word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party
man gives he, the male pronoun; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A Conservative takes up some fellow's idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposed explanation that awaits proof is a hypothesis.

clue.text: Mass strike?

parts.note: read not as workers walking out together but as a punch landing on the torso, the mass of the person

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass strike' suggests industrial action; the question mark says to read 'mass' as the trunk and 'strike' as a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A punch to the torso is a figure for a severe setback.

clue.text: Poet's disagreement leading to quarrel over article that's cut

parts.note: to have words is to argue

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word for quarrel is turned upwards

parts.note: a row is a quarrel

indicators.note: the article is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A poet's argument escalates into a row about a piece of writing that was censored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROW into WOR; 'that's cut' trims THE to TH. The 's after Poet means 'is', linking to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was the English Romantic writer of the Lake District.

clue.text: Stop working for excise

explanation.surface: Someone stops working to deal with a tax on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that fails abruptly stalls, and to remove a passage is to snip it away.

clue.text: Trainee British engineer originally dismissed unfairly

indicators.note: unfairly suggests the remaining letters are dealt out wrongly, out of order
the original, or first, letter of engineer is sent away

explanation.surface: A British apprentice engineer was sacked without just cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally dismissed' drops the E from ENGINEER, and 'unfairly' rearranges NGINEER into EGINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or learner is someone just starting out.

clue.text: I haven't time to be overwhelmed

explanation.surface: Someone too busy to stop feels swamped.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PRESSED, it is what a busy person says.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard-pressed means having no spare moments; being deeply struck with admiration is the other sense.

clue.text: Old copper removed object

parts.note: far removed means distant
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: An elderly policeman has an item taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is a coin: the farthing was a British copper coin worth a quarter of a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: This quarter-penny piece, minted in bronze and earlier copper, was withdrawn in 1961.

clue.text: Whale noise enthralling Australian islander

parts.note: an orca is the killer whale

indicators.note: the noise holds the other piece captive inside it

parts.note: din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: The sound of whales captivates a visitor from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orcadian comes from Orkney, the islands off the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Orkney is an inhabitant of that archipelago.

clue.text: Do send a message to discover situation

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle, or con, them
to text is to send a message by phone

explanation.surface: Sending a message to find out where someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: The surrounding circumstances of an event are its setting.

clue.text: Suit that's always packed with others

definitions.text: Suit that's always packed with others

parts.words: Suit that's always packed with others
parts.note: describes a playing-card suit, which always sits in a pack alongside the other three suits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests clothing put in a suitcase; here it is one of the four card suits, always found in a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits in a deck, marked with black leaf-shaped pips.

clue.text: County group perch up above

indicators.note: above places one piece over the other in a down answer
in a down clue up means the word for perch is written upwards

parts.note: a rod, or perch, is an old unit of length
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A group of people go fishing for perch upriver in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROD into DOR, which goes above SET. Dorset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is one of the shires on England's southern coast.

clue.text: It's potentially explosive — it may end badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of it may end are arranged wrongly

explanation.surface: A tense situation which might finish in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A blasting explosive, used figuratively for anything sensational.

clue.text: Opera music's starting soon

indicators.note: starting points to the first letter of music

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: The music of an opera is about to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Manon is an opera by Massenet.
explanation.definitionFit: Manon, by Massenet, is a French work for the stage.

clue.text: Crackpot directions I carry out without resistance

parts.note: W is the compass direction west
E is the compass direction east
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to do a task is to carry it out

explanation.surface: An eccentric gives directions that I follow without any objection.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or odd person is a crank.

clue.text: Region that's quasi-autonomous in part

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the words quasi-autonomous is used

explanation.surface: An area which governs itself to some degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, a large area of the world.

clue.text: Resistance a German encounters, showing restraint

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: A German meets opposition and holds back.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap used to control a horse, and figuratively any check on behaviour.

clue.text: Determined sibling involved in plan

indicators.note: the sibling is involved in, or placed inside, the plan

parts.note: an intent is a plan or purpose
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A resolute brother or sister takes part in a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps demanding something is persistent and firm.

clue.text: Watch flag going round rope endlessly

indicators.note: the flag goes round, enclosing, the shortened rope

parts.note: a standard is a flag

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for rope loses its last letter

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to secure a tent

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the flag as it twists around a rope without its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims GUY to GU, which goes inside STANDARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep watch is to act as a sentry.
